title: Traces of the Other: Are DMT Entities Real? Donald Hoffman and Andrew Gallimore in Conversation
description:
Could DMT temporarily transform the human perceptual interface, making conscious agents that are normally invisible to us perceivable?

Donald Hoffman and Andrew Gallimore examine this extraordinary question through neuroscience, mathematics, and the possibility that what we perceive is only a limited interface with a deeper reality, developing a framework that could be tested empirically.

This conversation marks the first public partnership of the Trace Institute Collaboration Program, developed with Noonautics and moderated by Charles Yokoyama.

Subscribe to the Trace Institute for new research, films, and conversations exploring consciousness and the fundamental nature of reality.

EXPLORE THE RESEARCH

Read the paper and explore the Trace × Noonautics collaboration: https://traceinstitute.org/collaborations/gallimore/

Visit the Trace Institute: https://traceinstitute.org/

The Trace Institute is a non-profit research organization with a mission to build a science of
reality based on mathematical modeling of conscious observers. Founder and Scientific
Director Donald D. Hoffman is Professor Emeritus at the University of California-Irvine, who
developed the interface theory of perception, conscious agent theory, and the trace logic of
conscious realism, among the first unified, observer-centered models of nature.

Learn more about Noonautics: https://noonautics.org/

Noonautics is a 501(c)(3) non-profit research organization supporting public-facing research
into the structure of the mind and the nature of non-ordinary experience. Director Andrew R.
Gallimore is a pioneer of DMT research and co-inventor of the DMT extended state
pharmacokinetic model, termed DMTx, with Dr. Rick Strassman. He is based at the Okinawa
Institute of Science & Technology

ABOUT THE CONVERSATION

What if the world we perceive is not reality itself, but a species-specific interface shaped by evolution?

Donald Hoffman’s theory of conscious realism proposes that conscious agents and their interactions are fundamental, while spacetime and physical objects are representations within a perceptual interface.

Andrew Gallimore’s research asks whether DMT can temporarily transform that interface, allowing human observers to experience structures or conscious agents that are ordinarily inaccessible.

Together with mathematician Niffe Hermansson, Hoffman and Gallimore have developed a formal framework intended to generate predictions that can be investigated and potentially falsified.

Recorded on June 13, 2026, at The Lighthouse Campus in Los Angeles.

FEATURING

Donald Hoffman
Cognitive scientist, co-founder of the Trace Institute, and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Irvine

Andrew Gallimore
Neurobiologist, pharmacologist, author, and founder of Noonautics

Moderated by Charles Yokoyama
Trace Institute researcher and former Senior Scientific Editor of Neuron

#DonaldHoffman #AndrewGallimore #Reality #DMT #Philosophy #Neuroscience #Psychedelics #Science #TraceInstitute #TracesOfTheOther #Consciousness

description:
What are UFOs—and why do so many encounters seem to involve consciousness, altered states, perception, and non-human intelligence?
In this special episode, four of my favorite thinkers ever to appear on Third Eye Drops offer different, but complementary takes on the phenomenon, UFOs and consciousness.

Dr, Donald Hoffman, cognitive scientist and idealist philosopher, explores the possibility that spacetime is only a perceptual headset—and that UAP may be operating from a deeper level of reality outside the interface.

Dr. Bernardo Kastrup, philosopher and leading advocate of analytic idealism, considers whether UFOs and entities could emerge from autonomous regions of mind, neighboring domains of consciousness, or intelligences that do not fit neatly into physical space.

Dr. Jeffrey J. Kripal, scholar of religion and the paranormal, examines the phenomenon as simultaneously physical, psychic, symbolic, and deeply entangled with human imagination, culture, and meaning.

Dr. Andrew Gallimore, neurobiologist and researcher of entity encounters, proposes that non-human intelligences may access or manipulate the brain’s world-building machinery, constructing entire experiential realities and appearing through forms or “masks” the mind can perceive.

Together, these four perspectives challenge the conventional extraterrestrial hypothesis and point toward something far stranger: a phenomenon that may sit at the intersection of mind, matter, perception, and reality itself.

title: Erzeugt das Bewusstsein das Gehirn? Was belegt ist und was nicht
description:
Donald Hoffman geht einen Schritt weiter als die Forschung, auf die er sich beruft. Er sagt, nicht das Gehirn erzeuge das Bewusstsein, sondern das Bewusstsein bringe das Gehirn hervor.

Wichtig dabei: Das ist seine theoretische Position und keine belegte Erkenntnis. In der Neurowissenschaft widersprechen ihm viele, weil sich Bewusstsein bislang nur zusammen mit Vorgängen im Gehirn beobachten lässt.

Denken darf man den Gedanken trotzdem. Er zeigt, wie wenig wir über die Entstehung von Bewusstsein tatsächlich wissen.

Das ganze Gespräch und die Einordnung stehen im langen Video auf diesem Kanal:
